body.text: Donald Trump hails 'great friendship' with Xi Jinping as Chinese leader visits White House
Pomp and pageantry were on full display as Donald Trump welcomed Xi Jinping to the White House for the first time in more than a decade.
Scores of military personnel holding Chinese and US flags greeted the Chinese president before Mr Trump guided Mr Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, to the rose garden for a military review and flyover.
As the lavish reception got underway, Mr Trump praised his "truly great friendship" with the Chinese leader, saying together they had "made tremendous strides on the issues facing our two countries".
Mr Xi confirmed he too was there to "carry on our friendship", announcing two pandas — a traditional symbol of Beijing's diplomacy — would arrive at a zoo in Atlanta soon.
"China, US cooperation may not solve every problem in the world, but without our cooperation, it would be hard to solve many of the world's problems,"
AI must remain under 'human control', Xi says

But Mr Trump has warned "pressing" issues would be discussed during the three-day summit, including "security, technology and super intelligence", a term Mr Trump has started using to refer to artificial intelligence.
"The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come," the US president said at the White House.
He said while AI would be discussed, he wanted "to leave it exactly where it is".
"That is China's position also," Mr Trump said.
Yet Mr Xi said that Washington and Beijing had a responsibility to "develop and manage AI for good".
"And ensure that the development of AI is always under human control," he added.
Mr Xi added that the two countries had a "historic responsibility of advancing human development and progress" and should "strengthen communication".
Leaders of US AI companies and tech executives are expected to attend the state dinner on Thursday night, local time.
Xi calls for better dialogue with US military
A B-2 bomber and four fighter jets soared over the White House as Marines performed rifle tossing and formations during a military review was held in the White House's Rose Garden.

Smaller in scale than the troop review Mr Xi prepared for Mr Trump in Beijing in May, the US version held in the White House's Rose Garden paid homage to 250 years of America, with musicians dressed in colonial wear and white wigs.
The military was also a topic Mr Xi was keen to discuss.
"We can certainly find the right path for two great countries to get along on this planet we both call home," he said at the White House.
He said the US and China "must hold the line of no conflict and no confrontation" and called for better and more regular communication between the two militaries.

"China and the United States are different in national condition, but through candid, in-depth, and continued dialogue, our two countries can understand each other better, seek common ground, while shelving differences and build up mutual trust."
Iran, Taiwan brought up during White House talks
Mr Xi has called on the United States and Iran to resolve "issues through negotiation as soon as possible", during their bilateral meeting, according to a readout in Chinese state media Xinhua.

Mr Trump has previously tried to argue that China, which is heavily reliant on Gulf oil, should use its pull with Tehran to help end the conflict, but Mr Xi reportedly told Mr Trump during their talks that he supported the US and Iran returning to a June deal that would not only end the war but reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Mr Xi also urged the US president to show "prudence" on another conflict, and oppose Taiwan independence.
China has long asserted territorial ownership of Taiwan, a democratically governed island that relies on US power to counter Beijing's threats.
Ahead of the summit, China's defence ministry had warned the US to take "extreme caution" over arms sales to Taiwan.

"It should be emphasised that the Taiwan question is the most important in China-US relations and maintaining peace and stability in the Taiwan Strait is the greatest common issue of the two countries," ministry spokesperson Jiang Bin told the media.

The Trump administration approved a US$ 11 billion (AUD$15.6 billion) arms package for Taiwan in December, but a second package worth about US$14 billion has been held up for months, with Mr Trump calling it a "very good negotiating chip".
Henrietta Levin — a senior fellow at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies — told ABC's The World it was those comments that made "Beijing really excited".
"Because they potentially have an opportunity to get concessions on these really big strategic questions that are at the top of China's list of priorities," she said.
"That in the past would have been very difficult to get any movement from Washington on."

US and Chinese officials have also been working to encourage a more balanced trading relationship between the two countries, including new market access for American farmers, according to Mr Trump on Thursday.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has already said China and the US would continue their trade truce for another two months, but it has been widely hinted that there could be an announcement on further de-escalation of the trade war between the two countries, which could include lowering tariffs on non-sensitive goods.
Mr Xi said he welcomed US companies that wanted to invest and do business in China and hoped Chinese companies would be "treated fairly" in the US.
China could hold the power this visit
Ms Levin also said Xi likely had the power to "manoeuvre" the US this visit.
"For the US to go so far out of its way to show one of its chief adversaries a good time in Washington is quite a striking thing to see,"
She said the summit would largely be about "symbolism" rather than substance, adding the world was "yet to see whether progress is really achievable".
"There will be a lot of pomp for sure, but there are really important issues on the agenda too," she said.

"You can bet that the Chinese side is going to be very focused on what China calls Mr Xi's political dignity; very focused on the optics on handshakes, on food, on just how the meeting will feel, and therefore, how the bilateral relationship will feel overall.
"Xi wants to make sure Trump doesn't do anything that would make China's economy have an even harder time; he wants to keep the US out of Taiwan, out of Asia to the degree that it can.
"I think China's quite confident that they will be able to manoeuvre the United States into a kind of stability that is ultimately favourable to China."
No press conference scheduled amid feud with media
The summit schedule does not include a joint news conference, giving journalists a chance to ask questions.
The summit comes as US networks boycott White House pool coverage in protest of Mr Trump stripping credentials from MS Now, Politico and CNN.
The bilateral Oval Office meeting between Mr Trump and Mr Xi was scheduled to be closed to the press, but photographers were allowed in at the last minute to capture images.
In front of those cameras, Mr Trump remarked that Mr Xi had the friendliest press in the world.
The White House denied requests from the rest of the pool, including reporters who would be asking questions, to join.
When Mr Xi met former US President Barack Obama in 2015, they held a joint press conference as part of the White House summit.
